candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Firewall rules staged on the origin and verified from a second authenticated SSH session before the applying session is closed

journeys.name: origin-lockdown-verification
assertions: requests through Cloudflare return 200 for app-juli.com, demo.app-juli.com and api.app-juli.com
a direct request to the origin IP bypassing DNS is refused at the network layer
port 22 remains reachable from a second SSH session before the applying session is closed
certbot renew --dry-run succeeds for every hostname after the rules are applied
the Cloudflare IP range list refreshes automatically and a stale list cannot silently reject proxied traffic
uptime.yml continues to pass against the public hostnames

migrationCompatibility.notes: No database change. This is a host firewall change plus a runbook correction; the alembic revision graph is untouched.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not apply the rules. The origin remains reachable directly, which is the current (exposed) state — no regression, the vulnerability simply stays open.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Flush the added rules to restore reachability. If SSH is lost, recover through the Hetzner web console, which is the sole out-of-band path — root password authentication is disabled, so SSH keys are the only remote access. A second authenticated session MUST be held open while applying, and rollback must be rehearsed before the applying session is closed.

acceptanceCommands: python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k 'cloudflare or origin_lockdown or firewall'
doNotInfer: an agent can apply this — no agent has SSH access to the origin; application is manual and operator-driven

certbot HTTP-01 renewal is unaffected in all cases — it survives because Let's Encrypt reaches the origin through Cloudflare, but any grey-clouded or newly added unproxied hostname breaks renewal silently and surfaces ~60 days later as an expired certificate
this hardens anything beyond inbound 80/443 — SSH, DNS-01 migration, mTLS and Cloudflare dashboard configuration are all explicitly out of scope
the runbook already documents the Cloudflare topology — it documents direct-to-origin A records and is corrected by this issue
